parts.text: "Here is a research idea, the card a planner wrote for it, and a check of which existing research or industrial programmes would use its result, with the gaps that check found. Root question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures? Idea: {\"title\":\"Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer)\",\"text\":\"Enumerate binding modes of engineered capsid libraries against the BBB receptor panel (LY6A, LY6C1, ALPL, LRP6, CA4, AAVR) with docking, MD refinement, and AlphaFold-Multimer to test whether transcytosis-competent pairs share a geometric motif such as 3-fold-axis engagement of GPI-anchored receptors (https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/POSTER-Voyager_ASGCT_2024_FINAL_Ishan.pdf). Published modeling covers only single-digit complexes, e.g. AlphaFold-Multimer models of LRP6 with AAV-X1 and CAP-Mac VR-VIII peptides (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518), against an experimental catalog of ~150 AAV capsid structures (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12682079). Narrowing: This leaves aside everything after binding — endosomal sorting, lysosomal degradation, nuclear import — so the computed interface geometry stands in for the binding step alone, not for fate. Its answer still moves the root question because it either widens or closes the catalog of candidate signatures (Q3) against which the sufficiency claim (Q1) must be tested.\",\"root_link\":\"Bears on Q3 of the root question — for which capsid–receptor binding signatures transcytosis occurs — specifically whether a shared interface motif marks transcytosis-competent complexes.\",\"compute_open\":\"More parallel compute would buy model runs (capsid × receptor × pose); published measurements of its effect stop at single-digit numbers of AAV–receptor complexes modeled per study — two LRP6 peptide complexes in https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518 — and above that it is unknown whether exhaustive enumeration would surface a shared transcytosis-competent motif or demonstrate that no such motif exists.\",\"sequential\":\"none: every capsid–receptor pair is an independent docking or AlphaFold-Multimer job with its own random seeds, so the work already splits into independent pieces.\"} Card: **Option 1: Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer) · Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer).** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: not the lever · PASS **Question.** Does exhaustive modeling of AAV capsid–receptor complexes reveal a shared interface motif, like 3-fold-axis GPI-receptor engagement, that marks which capsids transcytose the BBB? **What is known.** The earlier APPRAISE-AAV study used AlphaFold-Multimer, ten replicate models per matrix, to rank capsid peptides against the receptors LY6A, LY6C1 and CA4, validating one PHP.eB–LY6A pose [s_appraise]. Whether a shared 3-fold-axis GPI-engagement motif marks transcytosis-competent pairs across a whole capsid panel, or whether deeper pose sampling changes that call [s_appraise]. **Hypothesis.** Transcytosis-competent capsids engage GPI-anchored BBB receptors at the capsid 3-fold spike with a shared anchor geometry, unlike non-cognate pairs [s_appraise]. **If compute is the lever.** At 2,880 models the competent-minus-retained GPI-engagement gap reaches 0.50 or more, while at 144 models it stays below 0.25. **If not.** The gap stays within 0.15 of its 144-model value at every depth; added poses change nothing because insert location already fixes the 3-fold site [s_cat]. **Test.** Run 72 pairs at 144, 720, 2,880 pose models on 8x A100s [s_lambda], anchored on the published PHP.eB–LY6A complex [s_appraise]; compare with the ten-model published baseline and the 144-model shallow arm against phenotype labels [s_alpl]. *Compute axis.* Capsid–receptor pose models computed per panel sweep (rigid-docking poses plus AlphaFold-Multimer seed models): 144–2,880 pose models, 3 levels. Closest prior: 10 [s_appraise_rep], beyond it. *Restructuring.* none. **Check first.** Rebuild the published PHP.eB peptide–LY6A complex and require its validated contacts and capsid fit before any library spend [s_appraise]. Tolerance: capsid-fragment RMSD to PDB 7WQO at most 1.5 Å (published engineered-loop RMSD is 1.36 Å) and at least 2 of the 3 named contacts (peptide Pro5', Phe6', LY6A Ala58) within 5 Å. **Would not show.** Predicted interface geometry only, not transcytosis rates or post-binding fate; weak avidity-dependent contacts may evade prediction [s_appraise]; twelve capsids, six receptors. *Cost.* Plans $955.84 of the $1,000 budget over 59 machine-hours, leaving $44.16. Main guess: wall minutes per AlphaFold-Multimer seed job [g], measured after $51.74 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 1.1× higher. 2 cost flags in the block. Card verdict: PASS 1/2 Programme check: [{\"name\":\"Voyager Therapeutics — TRACER capsid discovery and ALPL NeuroShuttle (VCAP-102 / VY1706)\",\"step\":\"Mechanism-of-action step of the TRACER pipeline the card targets: after RNA-guided in vivo capsid evolution, Voyager identifies the vascular receptor each capsid uses to cross the BBB and demonstrates that binding of that receptor initiates transcytosis rather than mere uptake — i.e., the transcytose-versus-retain call per capsid–receptor pair. In practice this is done with human surface-protein binding/transduction screens, SPR, and a polarized cell-barrier Transwell assay, not with exhaustive structural enumeration.\",\"sum\":10},{\"name\":\"Gradinaru Lab (Caltech) / APPRAISE-AAV — receptor-directed AAV engineering and the open-source APPRAISE package\",\"step\":\"The computational step the card scales: ranking engineered capsid insertion peptides against BBB receptors by AlphaFold-Multimer pairwise competition modeling, scored with atom-counting energy plus binding-angle and pocket-depth geometry, used to classify receptor-dependent vs receptor-independent capsids and to pick candidates before in vivo selection. Today this runs at ten models per competition on single-GPU Colab sessions; the card asks whether 144–2,880 pose models per pair change the transcytosis call.\",\"sum\":15},{\"name\":\"Dyno Therapeutics — multi-mechanism BBB-crossing capsid portfolio (ALPL, TfR1, Dyno-discovered receptors)\",\"step\":\"The step the card targets is Dyno's mechanism assignment and structure-aware design for its CNS portfolio: deciding which BBB receptor each engineered capsid engages and whether that engagement crosses the BBB, then engineering capsids for several BBB-crossing mechanisms in parallel (ALPL, hTfR1, and Dyno-discovered receptors) rather than one pathway. Dyno states it integrates sequence- and structure-based approaches in its generative design, with receptor mechanism confirmed by head-to-head in vivo comparisons.\",\"sum\":9}] Gaps found: [\"No published pose-depth (model-count) scaling study for AAV capsid–receptor complexes exists; the closest comparators are 10 AF-Multimer models per competition (Ding et al. 2024) and 5 models with up to 20 recycles for LRP6 complexes (Shay et al. 2024), so the card's 144–2,880 arms have no prior baseline beyond the ten-model published one.\",\"Per-pair transcytose-versus-retain phenotype labels are scarce: Voyager's MDCK Transwell result covers VCAP-102±ALPL vs AAV9 only, and most programs (Dyno, Capsida, Gradinaru) score in vivo brain transduction rather than transcytosis rate, so the card's training labels may rest on few direct measurements.\",\"APPRAISE-style modeling uses isolated VR-VIII peptides (AA587–594), not the full 60-mer capsid at the 3-fold spike with GPI anchor and membrane; a 'shared 3-fold motif' may partly reflect the peptide-competition setup, and weak avidity-dependent contacts can evade prediction (the card's own caveat).\",\"Species gaps limit motif generality: LY6A/LY6C1 are mouse-restricted (absent in primates), 9P31/9P36 bind mouse but not primate CA4, while ALPL is conserved — a motif validated on mouse GPI receptors may not transfer to human-relevant pairs.\",\"Dyno's and Capsida's structural pipelines are proprietary, so 'already done' cannot be settled for them; Capsida's NR001–NR005 human BBB-receptor platform with plate-/bead-based capsid/receptor binding assays (capsida.com) and Lir's Starfish capsid-structure/docking pipeline (lirtx.com) are additional consumers of this result that were not assessed in depth here.\"] Propose three close variants of the idea. Each changes one thing (the system studied, the quantity more compute buys, the comparison it is judged against, or the programme it is aimed at) so that its result would matter more to a named programme or close a named gap. Keep the rest of the idea. Name only systems, tools and programmes that appear above or that you are sure exist. Decide only from the text above; do not use tools. Return only JSON: {\"variants\": [{\"id\": \"V1\", \"title\": \"\", \"text\": \"the idea in three to five sentences, in the form of the original\", \"root_link\": \"\", \"compute_open\": \"\", \"sequential\": \"\", \"changes\": \"what differs from the original and which gap or programme it answers\", \"narrowing\": \"what of the root question this leaves aside, what the computed observable stands in for, and why its answer still moves the root question; one to three sentences\"}]}"

Let me craft three variants, each changing one thing, grounded in the text.

Gaps to close or programmes to target:
- Gap: no pose-depth scaling study; closest comparators 10 AF-Multimer models (Ding et al 2024) and 5 models up to 20 recycles (Shay et al 2024).
- Gap: per-pair transcytose-vs-retain labels scarce; Voyager MDCK Transwell covers VCAP-102±ALPL vs AAV9 only.
- Gap: APPRAISE uses isolated VR-VIII peptides (AA587–594) not full 60-mer capsid at 3-fold with GPI anchor and membrane.
- Gap: species — LY6A/LY6C1 mouse-restricted; 9P31/9P36 bind mouse but not primate CA4; ALPL conserved.
- Gap: Capsida NR001–NR005 platform, Lir Starfish docking pipeline unassessed consumers.
- Programmes: Voyager TRACER/ALPL NeuroShuttle (VCAP-102/VY1706), Gradinaru/APPRAISE, Dyno.

Variant 1: change the system studied — full 60-mer capsid with GPI-anchored receptor and membrane patch at the 3-fold spike, anchored on PHP.eB–LY6A (PDB 7WQO), instead of isolated VR-VIII peptides. This closes gap 3 (peptide vs full capsid). Aimed at APPRAISE/Gradinaru and Voyager.

Variant 2: change the comparison it is judged against — instead of phenotype labels which are scarce, judge against paired Transwell transcytosis measurements on a human BBB model using ALPL (conserved) with VCAP-102/VY1706 and AAV9 as retained control; i.e., benchmark against Voyager's MDCK Transwell-like assay, and use human-relevant receptor ALPL to close species gap. Actually that changes the system AND comparison. Better: change comparison = use Voyager's VCAP-102±ALPL Transwell pair as ground truth anchor, expanding the label set by measuring a matched panel on human ALPL in a polarized barrier assay. Hmm but this is hybrid.

Alternatively V2: change the quantity more compute buys — instead of pose count, buy recycles/convergence or the number of capsids (panel breadth) across the ~150 capsid structure catalog, with a fixed shallow pose depth, to test whether the motif generalizes across capsid families. That answers gap 1? Hmm.

Let me keep three clean single-change variants:

V1: system studied → full 60-mer capsid + GPI-anchored LY6A in a membrane patch at the 3-fold spike (not isolated AA587–594 peptide). Closes gap 3; matters to APPRAISE/Gradinaru (their peptide-competition setup) and Voyager (real capsid engagement).

V2: comparison judged against → replace scarce transcytosis labels with a matched human polarized-barrier Transwell panel built around Voyager's VCAP-102 ± ALPL vs AAV9 result, using ALPL (conserved) plus a human-relevant receptor; i.e., judge the motif against transcytosis rate measured in the same assay. Closes gaps 2 and partially 4 (species). Aimed at Voyager TRACER/VY1706 and Dyno.

Hmm, but "keep rest of idea" — the idea is structural enumeration. V2 keeps modeling but changes the benchmark. That's allowed: "the comparison it is judged against."

V3: programme aimed at → Capsida (NR001–NR005 human BBB-receptor platform) and/or Lir Starfish, adapting the enumeration to their plate/bead capsid–receptor binding data, so the result tests motif against binding assays that exist across the receptor panel. Closes gap 5 (unassessed consumers). Or target Dyno's multi-mechanism portfolio (ALPL, TfR1) — requires naming TfR1 (appears above) and asking whether a shared motif vs mechanism-specific geometry. TfR1 isn't in the receptor panel though; adding TfR1 changes the system.

Better V3: change the quantity more compute buys — instead of pose models per pair, buy breadth across the ~150 AAV capsid structure catalog (or across the 6 receptors) at fixed shallow depth, testing whether any shared motif exists across capsid families rather than whether deeper poses reveal it. That directly addresses gap 1 (no scaling baseline) differently? Actually it addresses gap 1 by making the depth axis a fixed control. Hmm, but gap 1 says no prior pose-depth baseline — the original's compute-open premise. Better to have a variant that targets that: change the comparison to a two-point calibration against the published 10-model and 5-model/20-recycle baselines, i.e., judge the motif call at 10 and 5-model depths vs 144–2,880, so the result is an actual pose-depth scaling curve benchmarked to published practice. That's a comparison change and closes gap 1. But V2 already uses comparison change. The instructions say each changes one thing; multiple variants can change the same axis type as long as distinct. But better to diversify.

Let me do:

V1: system studied (full capsid + membrane-embedded GPI receptor, PHP.eB–LY6A 7WQO anchor) → gap 3, APPRAISE/Voyager.
V2: comparison judged against (Voyager VCAP-102±ALPL Transwell + AAV9, human ALPL polarized barrier) → gaps 2 & 4, Voyager/Dyno.

Alternative V3: programme aimed at Capsida's NR001–NR005 human BBB-receptor platform with plate/bead capsid–receptor binding assays, using the human-relevant receptor set (ALPL, AAVR, LRP6) — closes gap 5 and species gap 4 partly. But that changes system too (receptor panel).

I think the instruction allows change of "the programme it is aimed at" — so V3: aim at Capsida/Lir, keep the modeling but output a ranked motif call matched to their binding-assay format (binary bind/no-bind plus geometry), evaluated against their NR001–NR005 panel readouts. Closes gap 5. That's a comparison/aim change.

Maybe do V3 as: change the comparison to the published shallow baselines — build the pose-depth scaling curve anchored at Ding et al. 10-model and Shay et al. 5-model/20-recycle depths, so the deliverable is the first published model-count scaling curve and the motif call at each depth. Closes gap 1. That's clean and distinct: "comparison it is judged against." But V2 also is a comparison. Fine — change axes: V1 system, V2 comparison/labels, V3 programme/consumer. Let's do V3 as programme aimed at Capsida + Lir with their assay formats. And V2 as comparison.

Actually let me reconsider making V2 = the pose-depth scaling baselines (gap 1) — that's very much in the spirit of the card (compute is the lever) and would matter to APPRAISE (which runs 10 models). And V3 = labels/species with Voyager ALPL Transwell. Hmm, V3 then changes both comparison and system (human ALPL). Let me put the species/label one at Voyager and keep it as "comparison it is judged against."

Final:

V2 — comparison: pose-depth scaling curve benchmarked to published 10-model and 5-model/20-recycle baselines; deliverable = model-count scaling curve; matters to APPRAISE.

But then no variant addresses gap 2/4 labels+species, which are juicy. Could fold species into V1 (use human-relevant receptor? no, LY6A is mouse).

I'll accept two comparison-axis variants but make them clearly different: V2 = comparison against published model-count baselines (gap 1); V3 = comparison against measured transcytosis labels in human barrier assay (gaps 2,4). The "one thing" for each is a single distinct change; they're distinct variants.

Actually, better to make V3 the programme-aimed one at Capsida, and instead squeeze labels/species into V2? V2: pose-depth scaling anchored to published baselines AND... no.

Let me just do four? No, three requested.

Reorder: V1 system (full capsid/membrane) — gap 3. V2 comparison (transcytosis labels on human ALPL barrier, Voyager VCAP-102) — gaps 2 & 4, programmes Voyager/Dyno. Alternatively V3 as "quantity more compute buys": buy breadth across the ~150 capsid structure catalog at fixed depth — tests generality across capsid families, matters to Dyno's multi-mechanism portfolio.
